content: The laboratory findings page should be titled with the disease name followed by laboratory findings, ensuring that only the first letter of the title is capitalized. The primary objective of this page is to provide a detailed description of the significant laboratory tests and findings associated with the disease being discussed. It is important to note that this section is not intended for describing imaging studies or other diagnostic modalities. At the top of the edit box, include the {{CMG}} template, your name template, and the microchapter navigation template that you created at the beginning. This is a standard requirement for all microchapter pages linking to the main page. When creating links within the page, use square brackets around key terms to link them to other relevant pages within Wikidoc. Ensure that the links are as specific as possible. For instance, if the text mentions anterior spinal artery syndrome, the link should direct to the page for anterior spinal artery syndrome rather than generic terms like anterior, artery, or syndrome. For further guidance on creating links, refer to the provided instructions. Follow the prescribed format and capitalization rules as outlined in the template. Additionally, the name of the disease should be included in the first sentence of every subsection. The overview section should begin with the disease name in the first sentence. This section aims to summarize the laboratory findings page in a concise manner, typically in a few sentences. It can mirror the laboratory findings segment from the overview page. For an example of an overview section on a laboratory findings page, refer to the provided link. In the template section, the first sentence should clearly introduce the laboratory findings. Examples and additional sentences can be included to provide clarity and context. If there are diagnostic laboratory findings associated with the disease, preferred template statements include: An elevated/reduced concentration of serum/blood/urinary/CSF/other is diagnostic of [disease]. Laboratory findings consistent with the diagnosis of [disease] include [specific findings]. [Specific test] is usually normal among patients with [disease]. Some patients with [disease] may have elevated/reduced concentrations of [specific marker], which is usually suggestive of [disease]. If there are no diagnostic laboratory findings associated with the disease, state: There are no diagnostic laboratory findings associated with [disease]. In the Laboratory Findings section, outline or list the relevant laboratory tests that should be performed for the disease being described. Clearly indicate what the expected laboratory findings would be. For an example of a laboratory findings section, refer to the provided link. You may include subheadings to describe specific types of laboratory tests, if applicable.
